Final New Zealand election vote count to confirm parliament make up

Reuters

27 November, 2026 03:00 am IST

WELLINGTON, Nov 27 (Reuters) – Final government election results are due to be released in New Zealand later on Friday, with the official count expected to confirm whether the incumbent centre-right government can hold on to its razor-slim majority.

Preliminary results released by New Zealand’s Electoral Commission after the November 7 election showed the incumbent three-party ruling coalition led by National had a majority of two seats, after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter disillusionment with the two biggest contenders.

The final results released on Friday will include around 400,000 special votes, which include ballots cast overseas and those requiring additional checks. Those votes have typically favoured the left, with parties on the right losing support following the count. This could also be key in seats where races remain tight between Labour and National candidates.

Show Full Article

Party leaders are expected to respond after the results are published, as negotiations over a possible governing arrangement gather pace.

Under New Zealand’s proportional representation system, parties frequently need support agreements with smaller partners to form an administration.

There are 71 constituency seats and at least 49 party seats, and a party or coalition needs a majority to form a government.

The final tally will also settle the number of electorate and list seats won by each party, providing a clearer picture of the balance of power for the next parliamentary term.

(Reporting by Lucy Craymer; Editing by Chris Reese)

BRUSSELS, Nov 26 (Reuters) – EU leaders will try to reach an agreement on the next long term budget for the EU this year, but will not reconvene for new talks on Friday, German chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday evening.

Merz said a day of talks between EU leaders in Brussels had brought “new movement” towards a reduction of the proposed size of the next budget, as demanded by Germany and other countries who are net contributors to the bloc’s finances.

The leaders will try to hammer out a deal during a two-day summit starting December 17, Merz said.

Show Full Article

The German chancellor repeated his stance that all 27 EU members should contribute to aid for Ukraine, and said this would be discussed further during a last round of talks between the leaders on Thursday evening.

(Reporting by Andreas Rinke, editing by Bart Meijer)

MARACAY, Venezuela, Nov 26 (Reuters) – Workers at Venezuela’s Amuay refinery evacuated on Thursday due to a fire in a trench containing residual products, although the blaze was extinguished with no injuries reported, according to five workers at state oil company PDVSA.

One worker said the incident led to the temporary shutdown of Distillation Unit 1, the only currently operational unit at Amuay, the largest refinery in the country and part of the Paraguana Refining Center in northwestern Venezuela.

PDVSA, which owns Amuay, confirmed in a statement that the fire was put out without causing injuries. It added the incident did not affect domestic fuel distribution. It did not address the status of the distillation unit or the cause of the fire.

Show Full Article

Another worker said the fire began in a naphtha pipeline when leaked fuel ignited, setting fire to a truck and other vehicles.

Fires and power outages are frequent at PDVSA refineries, which are in dilapidated condition and operate at a fraction of capacity.

Amuay has a processing capacity of 645,000 barrels per day but is currently processing only 67,000 barrels per day.

(Reporting by Mircely Guanipa in Maracay and Deisy Buitrago in Caracas, writing by Paolo Laudani, Editing by Natalia Siniawski and Daina Beth Solomon)

Nov 26 (Reuters) – As American families gathered to celebrate one of the biggest holidays of the year, US President Donald Trump on Thursday used the occasion of Thanksgiving to attack liberals, immigrants and a federal agency.

In a message on his Truth Social platform, Trump offered holiday greetings to people he accused of fraud, error or criminality.

“I would like to wish a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left,” Trump said in the 461-word post.

Show Full Article

The message was issued while the Republican president spent the family-oriented holiday at his Trump International Golf Club in West Palm Beach, Florida. He was expected to call US service members later on Thursday from his Mar-a-Lago estate.

In the holiday greeting, Trump accused his own government of falsifying US economic data. He warned of efforts by unnamed people to implement Muslim religious law and forcibly redistribute private property. He also described large numbers of US immigrants and people of Somali descent as jobless or criminal.

Trump offered no evidence for any of the claims, some of which repeated longtime talking points. The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The US president also defended his White House renovation projects, saying reporters and citizens had misunderstood them.

Trump’s Republican Party suffered heavy losses in the November 3 midterm elections and will cede control of both chambers of Congress in January.

(Reporting by Reuters Washington bureau; Editing by Sergio Non and Bill Berkrot)
